briefFidelity: FAIL, and the disagreement is the one I wrote down before I read the brief. Unprompted I named this a stack of sawn timber with sticks thrown over it, and listed geology as an explicitly SECOND, WEAKER reading. The brief asks for a core sample - pure horizontal section, no ground plane, no horizon, dense and stacked, FILLING THE FRAME EDGE TO EDGE with NO SINGLE ELEMENT DOMINATING. Four specific breaches. (1) The unbriefed diagonal batons: 1283437 is a small thin stack under a wide X of long sticks reaching almost corner to corner, the 512 single is the same X, and 1733538 is carried by one big pale cream diagonal slab. A baton cutting across beds is not bedding; it is what produced the timber reading instead of the sediment reading. (2) Not edge to edge: 1283437, 1835793, 1733538, 1310661, 1475115 and 1203347 all float centre-frame inside wide black margins; only 1243682, 1985692 and 1991107 approach the brief's fill. (3) Single elements dominate: the pale sand mass in 1203347 and 1475115, the cream diagonal in 1243682, the lone wide gold bar in 1310661. (4) The forbidden ground plane is reinstated - 1310661, 1203347, 1283437 and 1985692 each set an isolated bottom bar below a gap of black, which reads exactly as a horizon with a mass above it. Palette and banding are genuinely on brief; the object is not the section the brief commissioned.
composition: Strongly centre-weighted and axial, with a real focal hierarchy - normally the widest, most saturated gold bar, with the diagonal batons as a crossing secondary gesture. On general terms that hierarchy is a virtue, but the brief explicitly asked for an even section with no single element dominating, so here it is a violation rather than an achievement: 1475115's pale block takes roughly a third of its tile, 1733538 is one bright cream diagonal over a minor stack, 1310661 resolves to one wide gold bar under a void. The frame is used inconsistently - 1243682 and 1985692 bleed off both sides while 1835793 and 1283437 leave most of the tile black. Where the work does obey the brief and go even, it goes inert instead: 1366079 and 1991107 flatten into a field of stripes with no incident at all.
collectionCoherence: The strongest axis. Laid out together the twelve are unmistakably one project: same single primitive, same near-black warm ground, same two-family palette, same vertical accumulation on a shared centre axis. 1835793 at its sparsest and 1243682 at its densest still read as the same hand and the same rule set, and 1283437's stick-dominated tile still belongs beside 1310661's near-purely-horizontal one. Nobody would mistake any tile here for another folder.
palette: Chosen, and the closest thing to a clean pass on the sheet - it matches the brief almost term for term. The warm family runs umber through ochre, caramel, sand and pale cream; the cold slate band is genuinely present and doing structural work, carrying the settling greys in 1366079 and 1991107 and the grey top block of 1243682 under stress. The near-black ground supports rather than competes: it holds the golds of 1310661 and 1985692 without greying them, and the partial-alpha overlaps in 1203347 and 1561509 generate intermediate tones instead of mud. Contrast range is doing work rather than making noise.
seedVariation: These are twelve different works, not one work at twelve rotations, and the spread sits at about the upper limit before a project stops being one project. Density is the main axis: 1835793 is a near-empty scatter of hairline rules with four small gold bars, 1243682 and 1985692 are dense full-bleed slabs. Structure varies too - 1310661 is four detached blocks with a real gap, 1283437 is stick-dominated, 1475115 is a wide chunky block, 1366079 is a flat even striped field. Colour balance separates the gold-led 1561509 and 1985692 from the grey-led 1366079 and 1991107. 1835793 is the one that strains coherence - it reads as a weaker, thinner project than 1243682 rather than as a sparse member of the same one - but it does not break it.
thumbnailSurvival: Mostly passes, and it is the axis the work is best engineered for. At 120 the stacked silhouette survives intact and the twelve still read as twelve objects: 1243682 solid, 1310661 gapped, 1283437 crossed, 1985692 gold-heavy, 1366079 grey and flat. What is lost is the fine layer count and the thinnest rules - 1835793 collapses to a small floating cluster with almost nothing around it and is the one tile that stops being a work at browse size, and the hairlines in 1366079 and 1991107 disappear into the ground. The diagonals survive as faint pale threads rather than as objects, so 1283437's X reads at 120 but 1203347's does not. No tile is mush; the loss is thinning, not collision.
marketResponse: Visible, but it is NOT the change the brief claimed, and its sign is not even consistent between seeds. The brief: under drawdown the beds THIN and FEWER survive; in recovery the sequence thickens and more beds return. What the sheets show: 1283437 gains beds under stress, its thin airy neutral stack thickening into a denser striped column - the opposite of fewer surviving. 1310661 also densifies under stress, its four separated blocks packing tight into one contiguous mass and closing the black gap. 1243682 does lose beds under stress, but the survivors get CHUNKIER and greyer, not thinner, so it fails the other half of the same sentence. Only the recovery half lands consistently - 1243682, 1203347 and 1310661 all re-laminate into more and thinner layers. A state change that is legible but points the wrong way on the one testable dynamic claim in the brief has not been delivered.
tokenIdentity: Passes cleanly, and it is the axis the state rows handle best. Same seed across all three states is unarguably the same token: 1203347 keeps its distinctive T of a wide top bar over a heavy pale diagonal in neutral, stress and recovery; 1243682 keeps its full-bleed slab stack and its big cream diagonal throughout; 1310661 keeps its four-block gapped identity even when stress closes the gap; 1283437 keeps its narrow core under an X in all three. Nothing is replaced by another work under drawdown - the changes are to layer count, thickness and stick reach, never to the object.
artifacts: Bars run off the left and right tile edges in 1243682, 1985692, 1991107 and 1366079, and in the states sheet the 1243682 stress tile has its top grey block cut by the top edge - I cannot tell from the sheets whether that is intentional bleed or a shape overrunning the viewBox, and the inconsistency with the wide-margin tiles like 1835793 and 1283437 argues it is not a decision. The hairline rules in 1366079, 1991107 and 1835793 sit at the edge of visibility at 256 and vanish at 120. 1283437's recovery sticks run out of the bottom of the frame and are cut. No element collides into mush and the alpha overlaps read as deliberate translucency rather than as mistakes.
reasoning: The gate decided it. Before reading anything I described a woodpile - a stack of planks with sticks thrown across it - and named strata only as a weaker second reading; the brief commissioned a core sample and expressly forbade the ground plane, demanded edge-to-edge fill, and demanded that no single element dominate. The work breaches all three, and it breaches them through a whole population of elements the brief never asked for: the diagonal batons that dominate 1283437, 1733538 and the 512 single are the very thing that makes this read as timber rather than as section, and the isolated bottom bars under black gaps in 1310661, 1203347 and 1283437 put back the horizon the brief struck out. Independently, the one testable dynamic claim - beds thin and fewer survive under drawdown - is contradicted by 1283437 and 1310661, which both gain beds under stress, and only half-met by 1243682, which loses beds but thickens them. The palette is an exact hit, coherence is strong, identity across states is clean and it survives 120px, so this is accomplished work; it is not the work that was briefed, and the gate says accomplishment does not buy a pass.
wouldChange: Three concrete things. First, remove the rotated batons entirely, or demote them to bed-thickness-scale intrusions that sit inside the section - as they stand they are the loudest gesture in 1283437, 1733538 and 1203347 and they are what makes the work read as thrown lumber instead of as a core sample. Second, drive the beds to the frame edges and kill the isolated bottom bar: extend every band past the viewBox on both sides so the section is cropped by the frame the way a real core sample is, and close the black gaps in 1310661 and 1283437 that currently manufacture a horizon; that also removes the dominant-element problem in 1475115 and 1733538, since a band that runs edge to edge cannot read as an object. Third, invert the stress response: under drawdown reduce bed COUNT and reduce bed THICKNESS together, so 1283437 and 1310661 thin out instead of densifying and 1243682's survivors get thinner rather than chunkier, and let recovery restore both. Keep the palette and the ground exactly as they are.
